subject: Private VPC sprint retrospective & architecture evidence
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, AtlasCloud Eng <eng@atlascloud.com>
Cc: NorthBridge Ops <ops@northbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC sprint retrospective & architecture evidence

Hi team —

Thanks for pulling time into the post-deploy retrospective this morning. Per our agenda, attaching the updated control-plane / data-plane diagram and the evidence checklist that Atlas requested during cutover. The two files summarize the changes we made during the sprint and the remaining low-risk action items.

Key notes:
- Control plane: moved to the regional control cluster with strict ingress from the management subnet only. See page 2 of controlplane-dataflow-v2.pdf for sequence diagram.
- Data plane: tenant pods remain in customer VLANs with NAT egress via the egress overlay; we added a stateless proxy to enforce per-tenant outbound rules.
- Observability: added explicit trace headers at the proxy boundary to preserve request provenance through the KV cache.
- Rollback path: we validated rollback in staging — documented steps 7–12 in the checklist.

Action items we agreed on in the call (owners in parens):
1) Finalize egress denylist proof artifacts and store in Drive (Irene).
2) Run the canary traffic profile for 48h and share latency heatmap (Jonas).
3) Update the deploy-runbook to include KMS key rotation notes for the control cluster (Marissa).
4) Provide AtlasCloud with a summary of the control/data separation and attestations (Dylan) — target EOD Wednesday.

Attachments: [attachment: controlplane-dataflow-v2.pdf (pdf)], [attachment: vpc-deploy-evidence-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Sr. Infrastructure PM
Redwood Inference

On Mon, 12 Apr 2027 at 09:02 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi team —
> 
> Thanks for pulling time into the post-deploy retrospective this morning. Per our agenda, attaching the updated control-plane / data-plane diagram and the evidence checklist that Atlas requested during cutover.

Thanks — quick notes from ops perspective after stepping through the checklist:

- The control-plane ALB health-check window needs to be loosened during large-model loads (we saw transient 504s at 90s headroom). I've annotated the checklist with the recommended 3x health-check interval.
- For the egress overlay: the proxy currently injects a small latency (6–12ms p95) when TLS is terminated/re-established for short-lived upstreams. Jonas, can you test whether we can reuse TLS sessions across the tenant pool?
- I confirmed that the KMS key used for signing deployment manifests is in the account's HSM; documented the ARN in the checklist.

I've attached an ops excerpt with suggested health-check and proxy tuning lines — paste into the runbook under the "runtime-tuning" section.

Attachments: [attachment: ops-excerpt-runtime-tuning.txt (txt)]

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Apr 12, 2027 at 11:18 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks — quick notes from ops perspective after stepping through the checklist:

A few security/compliance asks from my side before we hand off the final evidence bundle to Atlas:

1) Egress provenance: we need a signed artifact that shows per-tenant egress IP assignment for the 72-hour canary window (IP -> tenant mapping + timestamped logs). Can NorthBridge provide a short export of the NAT allocation for that time range? (cc: ops)
2) Control plane auth: confirm that service-to-service TLS is mTLS within the control cluster; provide the cert chain and rotation policy snippet to include in the evidentiary bundle.
3) Data retention: Atlas asked about metric/sample retention for the debug traces we keep for 7 days — we should produce a table mapping trace type -> retention policy.

I ran a quick scan of the controlplane-dataflow-v2.pdf and left comments on the Drive copy for two places where the boundary arrows weren't unambiguous (control->proxy and proxy->egress). I'll upload screenshots in the Drive thread.

If we can close items 1–3 by EOD Wednesday we should have a tidy bundle to attach to the SOW amendment.

Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick status update and next steps:

- Jonas has the canary plan running now (48h) and will send the latency heatmap by tomorrow morning.
- NorthBridge confirmed they can provide the NAT allocation export; ops@northbridge.com will drop the CSV to the Drive folder this afternoon.
- Marissa pushed the runtime tuning lines into the runbook (PR #189) and included the health-check changes.
- Irene: I'll assemble the cert-chain and rotation policy snippet and add the trace retention mapping to the checklist; target is EOD tomorrow.

I'll produce the final evidence bundle and upload a single PDF to the Drive root once all artifacts are in. Atlas — expect a short handoff email with the bundle and a one-page architecture summary by Thursday EOD.

If anyone sees a gap in the list above, flag it here and I'll pick it up. Otherwise I'll mark this thread as closed after upload.

Thanks,
Dylan
Sr. Infrastructure PM
